newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids fall on MGE collapse.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids fall on MGE collapse.

text.p: Bids for dark northern spring wheat were sharply lower on Thursday, matching near-limit losses in Minneapolis spring wheat futures, dealers said.
But some merchants said the collapse in wheat futures had farmers wary of further declines and was attracting some producer selling.
"Farmers are coming out and dumping some of their flat price grain," a Montana dealer said. "Guys are scared of the board so we've been buying a little bit of wheat."
North Dakota fields remained inundated with flood waters and producers were still weeks away from planting wheat.

"It is improving but we're not able to do a lot of work around here yet," a North Dakota dealer said. "We're looking at three weeks before farmers can get into the fields. Usually they're in the first week of May."

But farmers had not lost hope and few had opted to switch intended wheat acreage to soybeans, the merchant said. Soybeans can be planted later than wheat. USDA in March said North and South Dakota farmers would likely plant one million more acres of soybeans this year compared with last year due to heavy spring flooding.
